findings.title: FA1's generation guard (a read that settles after a clear cannot republish) has no test row: removing it survives every suite
findings.evidence: Extra mutant X5 deletes `if (gen !== generation) return null;` from the success arm of loadOnboardingResume's then: `[mut] X5 SURVIVED rc=0 start=2026-10-17 18:26:10 end=18:26:37 restore_sha=OK` against onboardingResume.b3a.test.tsx. My probe RV-S4 shows the guard matters and is correct at HEAD. It plants a record, defers the first getItem, calls clearOnboardingResume() while the preload is in flight, then releases the read. HEAD gives `[RV-S4] {peek0:{settled:false},peek1:{settled:true,value:null},peek2:{settled:true,value:null},storage:null,step:1}`. The same probe against X5 gives `[mut] X5P KILLED ... 18:51:26-18:51:40 restore_sha=OK` with `peek2:{settled:true,value:{step:3,data:{language:'ar'}}}, step:3`. Without the guard, the record republishes and a later mount resumes. In production this needs a logout or clear inside the first AsyncStorage round trip after bundle evaluation, so the user-facing effect is negligible. This is a regression-pin gap only. The committed code is correct.
